openQuestions.q: plan.md's CHK-007 section states its own DependsOn as only CHK-004, CHK-005, CHK-006, CHK-009, but the dependency-graph ASCII diagram at the bottom of the same plan.md draws explicit edges from CHK-010 and CHK-011 into CHK-007, and the Parallelism section separately states 'CHK-007 is last: it must observe the finished state.' CHK-010 and CHK-011 both write the same shared test file (red-b2aa7-artifact-validation.mjs) that CHK-007 re-runs for the post-fix invariance digest. Which is authoritative: should CHK-007's DependsOn text be corrected to add CHK-010 and CHK-011 (matching the diagram/prose intent), or is CHK-007 genuinely allowed to run before those two land?
openQuestions.evidence: plan.md CHK-007 section: '**DependsOn**: CHK-004, CHK-005, CHK-006, CHK-009'. plan.md dependency graph: 'CHK-004 ...-- CHK-006 -+ / ... +-- CHK-009 -+ / +-- CHK-010 -+ / +-- CHK-011 -+' all feeding into 'CHK-007'. plan.md Parallelism section: 'CHK-007 is last: it must observe the finished state.'
openQuestions.resolution: Accepted and corrected in plan.md. CHK-007 is the post-fix invariance assertion and must observe the finished state, so it has to wait on EVERY writer of the shared test file. Its DependsOn now reads CHK-004, CHK-005, CHK-006, CHK-009, CHK-010, CHK-011, which matches both the dependency diagram and the Parallelism section's statement that CHK-007 is last. The omission was an authoring slip from adding CHK-010 and CHK-011 after the graph was first drawn, not a deliberate scheduling choice.

openQuestions.q: CHK-010's plan.md section requires 'Run pre-fix AND post-fix; both must show the SAME behaviour for these rows... these must pass before the fix too' for its V2 and E4 regression rows, but CHK-010's own DependsOn is CHK-004 (the fix), so by the time an implementer is dispatched to CHK-010 the working tree already carries CHK-004's fix and there is no natural 'pre-fix' state left to observe. CHK-009 avoids this same problem because its pre-fix pin (row O2) is already written and committed by CHK-001 (dispatched before CHK-004) as part of CHK-001's own SILENT-class DoneWhen rows; no equivalent earlier item pins a pre-fix baseline for V2 (valid-v2-record-skip) or E4 (records-absent-UNSATISFIED). Should CHK-010's V2/E4 pre-fix rows instead be added to CHK-001 (dispatched pre-fix, mirroring how O2 was handled), should CHK-010's DependsOn be changed so it runs before CHK-004, should the implementer use the git-archive-replay technique already documented in red-w2c-v1-verdict-invariance.mjs's header comment, or is citing the decision document's own pre-existing §10.1/§10.2.1 [PROBE] evidence (captured before any of this story's code changed) sufficient to satisfy CHK-010's 'pass before the fix too' requirement without a fresh mechanical re-run?
openQuestions.evidence: plan.md CHK-010 section: '**DependsOn**: CHK-004' and 'Run pre-fix AND post-fix; both must show the SAME behaviour for these rows. Unlike CHK-001's rows, these must **pass before the fix too** - they pin behaviour that is already correct.' Compare plan.md CHK-001 DoneWhen, which explicitly lists '(row O2)' as one of its own SILENT-class pre-fix rows, and CHK-009 DependsOn CHK-004 with Verify text 'Pre-fix: satisfying-first-then-malformed returns SATISFIED with no throw - pin this first' referring back to that already-pinned row. No comparable CHK-001 row exists for V2 or E4.
openQuestions.resolution: Accepted as a genuine logic error on my part, and corrected. CHK-010 pins rows that must PASS before the fix (V2 and E4 are behaviour that is already correct), but I had scheduled it DependsOn CHK-004, i.e. after the fix has landed - at which point its own premise is no longer observable and the assertion would be vacuous. The parallel with CHK-009 does not hold: CHK-009's pre-fix O2 baseline is pinned by CHK-001, which is dispatched pre-fix, whereas nothing pinned a pre-fix baseline for V2 or E4. Corrected so CHK-010 now DependsOn CHK-001 and is authored pre-fix, serialised after CHK-001 because they share the test file, with CHK-007 re-running the rows post-fix as the actual regression proof. That is the same pre-pin then post-assert pairing already used by CHK-002 and CHK-007. plan.md additionally warns that CHK-001 and CHK-010 write rows with OPPOSITE pre-fix expectations into the same file - CHK-001's must FAIL pre-fix, CHK-010's must PASS - so they must sit in clearly separated labelled blocks.
